question: Should Georgia fully expand Medicaid eligibility to cover all eligible low-income adults
note: Registered voters, Jan 3-11 2024. Article says 'more than 69%' support; opposition share not reported in article. Republicans 47% support.

question: Support or oppose requiring nearly all adults to work or look for work to get Medicaid
note: National-only. Reverse-worded: sup = % opposing work requirements (38), opp = % supporting (62). Support fell to 32% when told about paperwork-driven coverage losses.

question: Support or oppose eliminating the 90% federal match for ACA Medicaid expansion adults
note: National-only. Reverse-worded: sup = % opposing the federal match cut (59), opp = % supporting it (40).

question: Should Congress increase, keep about the same, or decrease federal Medicaid spending
note: National-only. sup = increase (42); opp = decrease (17); 40% said keep about the same (so 82% oppose cutting).

question: Agree the state should expand Medicaid to cover more low-income and uninsured people
note: Registered voters, Nov 18-Dec 4 2024; strongly+somewhat agree. Opposition not reported in release.

question: Agree health costs are too high and the federal government should do more to negotiate cheaper prices
note: Registered voters. Federal negotiation framing; broad concept match for gov:drugbd. Opposition not reported.

question: Agree prescription out-of-pocket costs should be capped for insured adults
note: Registered voters. Broad prescription co-pay cap (closest to insulin co-pay cap piece of gov:priorauth); loose match for sen:priorauth. Opposition not reported.

question: Wisconsin should accept federal funds to expand Medicaid coverage
note: Registered voters, 2019 Marquette poll as reported by Wisconsin Watch; month, n and opposition not given in the write-up. Older poll, use as fallback.

sponsor: Florida Decides Healthcare (Medicaid expansion ballot campaign)
question: Support expanding Medicaid to adults 18-64 at or below 138% of poverty
note: Likely voters, June 11-17 2025. Sponsored by the campaign behind the proposed amendment.

question: Favor expanding Medicaid in Kansas (covering ~150,000 more, 90% federal cost)
note: Registered voters, Nov 10-20 2023. Sponsor is a pro-expansion health foundation; n and opposition not stated.

question: Support expanding Medicaid in Texas to cover more low-income uninsured people
note: Texas adults, Oct 18-Dec 19 2023. Nonpartisan health foundation sponsor. Opposition not stated in summary.

pollster: Texas Southern University Barbara Jordan Public Policy Research and Survey Center
question: Want the Legislature to expand Medicaid access this session vs keep status quo
note: Released March 2025; exact field dates and n not stated (fielded month approximate). opp = favor status quo; 18% unsure.

question: Support a state prescription drug affordability board that could limit what payers pay for high-cost drugs
note: Likely VA voters, June 25-July 8 2025. Bill match for gov:drugbd; concept for sen:drugneg. Up 9 pts from AARP 2023. Opposition not reported. AARP-sponsored; tier 2-3 judgment call.

question: Support or oppose federal legislation reducing or eliminating Medicaid coverage
note: Reverse-worded: sup = % opposing Medicaid cuts (63), opp = % supporting (25). Likely VA voters. AARP-sponsored.

question: Set upper payment limits on certain high-cost prescription drugs in New Hampshire
note: NH adults 18+, June 20-24 2024. Strongly 58 + somewhat 22 support; 8 neutral, 7 don't know. Concept match for sen:drugneg.

question: Support or oppose NH having a Prescription Drug Affordability Board
note: Strongly 33 + somewhat 26 support; somewhat 21 + strongly 3 oppose, per PDF extraction (oppose split looked odd, 13% listed as refused; verify before use). AARP summary says 'about 6 in 10' support.

question: Support letting Medicare negotiate prescription drug prices
note: Arizona registered voters, Sept 21-27 2021, online panel weighted. Release says 'over 94%' support; opposition not reported. Pre-IRA poll.

pollster: Lake Research Partners and Chesapeake Beach Consulting
sponsor: Americans for Financial Reform / Center for Responsible Lending
question: Support the CFPB rule removing medical debt from credit reports (after hearing CFPB rationale)
note: National-only, likely voters, online July 17-25 2024. Advocacy-sponsored. Republicans 78% support.

question: Support banning providers and collectors from reporting medical debt to credit bureaus
note: National-only. Article says 'more than 80%' and 'more than 1,300' voters; fielded summer 2025 (month approximate). Sponsor is a medical-debt relief nonprofit.

question: Legislators should set standards for insurer prior authorization decisions and require disclosure of PA rules and approval rates
note: Registered VA voters, Dec 17-20 (year inferred as 2024 from Jan 8 2025 article date); 4% undecided. Sponsor not named in article; may be advocacy-commissioned.

question: Favor requiring electronic prior authorization (also: response deadlines, public requirements 80%)
note: National-only adults, online, early Nov 2022. Electronic PA is the core of the Improving Seniors' Timely Access to Care Act. Patient-advocacy sponsor; 49% unfavorable vs 39% favorable toward prior authorization itself.

question: Mississippi should accept federal funds to expand Medicaid
note: Registered voters, Jan 8-12 2023 (year inferred from Jan 18 2023 article). Strongly+somewhat agree; Republicans 70%.

question: Favor expanding Medicaid to cover South Carolinians earning up to about $18,000 a year
note: June 21-30 (2021, inferred from Aug 3 2021 article). Article ambiguous whether 78% is all registered voters or those 50+; opposition not reported. Republicans 69%.

sponsor: ACS CAN, American Heart Association, American Lung Association, AARP
question: Support a described proposal to expand Medicaid coverage in Wyoming
note: Wyoming residents; field dates not reported (article Oct 19 2021). Question described a hypothetical expansion scenario. Health-advocacy sponsors.

sponsor: Michigan Health & Hospital Association, Michigan Association of Health Plans, CMH Association of Michigan, Michigan Primary Care Association, Protect MI Care
question: Oppose cutting Medicaid to pay for tax cuts
note: Field dates and n not stated (released during the 2025 federal budget debate). Also 83% want Medicaid spending increased or kept the same; 71% oppose cuts creating a state deficit. Health-industry/coalition sponsors.
